youtube_description:
Two boys grew up in the same neighbourhood in Kagoshima. One became Japan's most beloved hero. The other built the modern state, and in 1873 he chose it over his oldest friend. Okubo Toshimichi's government crushed Saigo Takamori's Satsuma Rebellion in 1877, and he was assassinated on the Kioizaka slope in Tokyo on May 14, 1878, at the age of 47. Follow time-travelling reporter Tokio Kamiya as he files dispatches from Kagoshima, Tokyo and the corridors of the Meiji government.

📰 Your reporter: Tokio Kamiya, a former Tokyo foreign correspondent. His grandfather's brass pocket watch carries him to one day of Japan's past at a time. He can watch and he can speak, but he can never change what happens. Every episode is his dispatch from the scene.

Six former samurai step out from the roadside. The horse is cut down, the coachman falls, and the minister is struck down on the road. Okubo is forty-seven. Saigo has been dead for less than eight months. I want to call out, but the rule of the watch is plain: I may not change a thing. The attackers carry a statement accusing him of shutting out the voice of the people. I take my hat off.
